newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea wet values firm, paper mixed, trade lifeless.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea wet values firm, paper mixed, trade lifeless.

text.p: North Sea physical crude was notionally firm but virtually inactive on Tuesday while paper was mixed and equally lifeless, traders said.
The sole physical trade heard was a mid-July Ekofisk moved at a 20 cent premium to benchmark Dated Brent, unchanged from Monday's trade of an July 8-10loader.
Outright values were a touch firmer, with August IPE Brent trading at $18.04 a barrel at 1205 GMT in a follow-through to technically-inspired late strength on Monday.
"It's dead. No one seems interested," one trader said of both physical and paper markets.
Market talk drew background support from a demand by Saudi Arabia and Iran at an OPEC meeting in Vienna that group members stop exceeding quotas and help buoy sagging outright prices.
Saudi Arabia also expressed confidence that rising demand for oil later this year ould support the market.
September/October Brent traded unchanged at -16 cents. July/August Brent changed hands at a little changed -15 cents.
Brent CFDs gave little direction and no trades were heard in morning talk. Next week was valued slightly softer at around August -33 cents, with July 7-11 at August -17 cents.
A Brent loading July 9-11 was due to turn wet. Shell UK is the equity holder.

Support for wet values derived from short-term tightness and uncertainty over the fate of the three or four Brents held by a European major. The company was rumoured to be examining all options but the arbitrage to the United States was looking poor.
Another prop came from news that the Nelson field in the Forties system is due to remain close to full output next week following repairs -- several days later than originally expected.
But deteriorating Western hemisphere refinery margins were seen undermining buying interest.
